result.title: Beyond Correct Answers: How Compositional Cues Shape Visual Judgments
result.summary: Visual question answering requires models to assign attributes and relations to the correct objects, a problem known as visual binding. Structured prompts make these assignments explicit through labeled fields. Yet an improvement from the full prompt does not reveal which labels help or how they interact. First, we isolate field-label effects across ten models and six tasks by holding the image and claim fixed. These comparisons reveal differences that overall accuracy can hide. With a relation label present, adding object-role labels helps Qwen3 but hurts Qwen2 on Spatial. Second, we compare auxiliary hints that preserve or swap the question's role assignments against a no-hint baseline. Across two image sets, Qwen3's advantage with preserving hints mainly reflects errors caused by swapped hints. Preserving hints remain near baseline. Field order further affects the harm. Third, we test clearer hint wording and direct selection of the relation shown in the image. Clearer hints improve text matching but do not consistently improve visual judgments. In contrast, relation selection partly reduces errors for some hints in Qwen3 and GPT-4.1-mini.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在固定图像与陈述的前提下，跨十个模型、六个任务系统比较结构化提示中的字段标签、辅助提示（保留或交换角色分配）、字段顺序及关系选择对视觉绑定判断的影响，并发现更清晰措辞主要改善文本匹配而非视觉判断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其字段级对照揭示模型依赖文本线索而非视觉证据（即视觉旁路），与 LVR 关注的实体-关系绑定、答案是否真正使用视觉内容直接相关，可供核查该诊断范式能否用于检验 latent 状态中的视觉信息贡献。
